binding_demand.concentration: Revenues from the two largest customers were ~19% and ~20% of total FY2025 revenue ($335.4M); customer identities anonymized as 'Customer D/E' in the 10-K's 10%-concentration table. Revenue mix FY2025: 46.9% national security, 21.6% civil, 31.5% commercial; 41.6% of revenue from customers outside the U.S. Backlog was $411.2M at 12/31/2025 (Space $299.8M, Defense Tech $111.4M), growing to $542.1M organic backlog at 6/30/2026; book-to-bill was 1.32x for FY2025 (Space 1.13x, Defense Tech 1.62x) vs 0.76x in FY2024, and organic backlog additions of $352.3M vs $214.0M revenue recognized in H1 2026 (~1.65x).

related_parties.customer_is_financier: Yes. AE Industrial Partners (AEI) - Redwire's founder and, until 2026, controlling preferred/common shareholder and Edge Autonomy's seller - also has portfolio companies that are Redwire customers (disclosed as 'Related Party A/B/C', linked via board interlocks with directors Kirk Konert, Reggie Brothers, James McConville and Frank Calvelli). AEI additionally financed the Edge Autonomy acquisition's cash consideration via a $100M related-party Seller Note (repaid in full June 2025) and via the original 2022 $81.25M Series A Convertible Preferred Stock investment (fully converted to common and sold by both AEI and Bain Capital by mid-2026).
related_parties.related_party_transactions: FY H1 related-party revenue: $2.321M (H1 2025) and $0.606M (H1 2026) from Related Party A/B/C combined; related-party AR of $0.437M at 6/30/2026. AEI's board nomination rights (up to 4 directors) were tied to its ownership; AEI's ownership fell below 1% during Q2 2026 and it 'was no longer considered a related party' as of 6/30/2026. Bain Capital (BCC Redwire Aggregator, L.P.) fully exited its preferred/common position in 2025; its board designee (Ray Wallander) resigned 2/11/2026 as the nomination right had expired.
related_parties.citation: 10-Q, 2026-08-06, same URL, Note Q - Related Parties: 'A customer of the Company, Related Party A, is a related party because Kirk Konert, a member of the Company's Board, also serves on the board of directors for the customer' and 'During the three months ended June 30, 2026, AEI's ownership of the Company significantly decreased to less than 1% and AEI was no longer considered a related party as of June 30, 2026.'

graveyard_gates.material_weakness: Yes, explicit and unremediated as of the most recent 10-Q. Management concluded disclosure controls were not effective as of both 12/31/2025 and 6/30/2026, citing ITGC gaps at Redwire Defense Tech (Edge Autonomy) and European operations, and insufficient time to demonstrate operating effectiveness of U.S. process-level controls.

reasons: Explicit, unremediated gate: management concluded disclosure controls were not effective as of both 12/31/2025 and 6/30/2026 due to material weaknesses (ITGC gaps at the newly acquired Edge Autonomy/European operations and unproven U.S. process-level controls), per 10-Q, 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000124/rdw-20260630.htm: 'certain of our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of June 30, 2026 due to the material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting described below.'

Demand is real but customer identity is opaque and concentrated: the two largest customers (~19% and ~20% of FY2025 revenue) are anonymized as 'Customer D/E' rather than named, even though backlog ($411.2M, growing to $542.1M) and book-to-bill (1.32x FY2025) show genuine, recognized-revenue demand, per 10-K, 2026-02-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000181981026000029/rdw-20251231.htm: 'Revenues from our two largest customers were approximately 19% and 20% of our total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.'

Heavy related-party insider distribution around the Edge Autonomy deal: AEI's Edge Autonomy-seller entity (AE Red Holdings, LLC) sold down from 19.7% (1/9/2026) to 1.1% (5/18/2026) of the company it had just been paid 49.76M shares to sell into, while acting as a related-party financier/customer-interlock, per SCHEDULE 13D/A, 2026-05-20, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819810/000110465926064511/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml: 'Percent of class represented by amount in Row (11) 1.1%.'
data_gaps: Q3 2026 activity (July-September 2026) is not yet reflected in a 10-Q; any ATM draws, contract awards, or insider transactions after 6/30/2026 (except the two 8-Ks and Form 4/144 filings explicitly checked in the filing index) were not independently verified beyond the filing index.

The two most recent Schedule 13G filings (2026-07-29 and 2026-08-07) were identified in the filing index but not fetched/read in detail; the specific institutional holder names and percentages are not confirmed in this research.

Form 4 transactions were not individually tabulated line-by-line for a precise 12-month buy/sell count; the conclusion of 'net selling' rests on the Form 144 volume and the 13D/A and DEF 14A ownership trend, which is directional but not a transaction-by-transaction tally.

Exact underwriting discount/commission percentage for the June 2025 follow-on offering (15,525,000 shares at $16.75) was not located in the excerpted text of the preliminary 424B5 (the final priced 424B5 filed 2025-06-17 was not separately fetched).

The full DEF 14A Item 13 'Certain Relationships and Related Transactions' narrative section (if present beyond the beneficial-ownership table and Note Q disclosures already cited) was not located/fully read in the proxy text extracted.

Backlog and customer-concentration figures for the Defense Tech/Edge Autonomy segment specifically pre-date the acquisition close (6/13/2025); FY2024 Defense Tech figures in the 10-K reflect only a partial-year/different-scope predecessor business, complicating pro-forma growth comparisons as flagged in the task.
